cards.explanation: The answer is True. These disciples tell Paul, “we have not even heard that there is a Holy Spirit.” (Acts 19:2) Paul asks one short question and gets that answer. I think he had more to say after that, and he did.

The answer is the baptism of John. The disciples answer Paul, “The baptism of John…” (Acts 19:3) Paul then says John's baptism was a baptism of repentance (Acts 19:4). I think that answer tells Paul right where to pick up the conversation.
The answer is Jesus. Paul says John “…told the people to believe in the One coming after him, that is, in Jesus.” (Acts 19:4) Paul names Him plainly, so nobody has to guess.

The answer is True. “On hearing this, they were baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.” (Acts 19:5) Paul explains, and they listen. They hear that John told people to believe in Jesus, and then they are baptized.

The answer is that the Holy Spirit comes on them and they speak in tongues and prophesy. The text says, “…the Holy Spirit came upon them, and they spoke in tongues and prophesied.” (Acts 19:6) It all happens right after Paul lays his hands on them. Plain and powerful, with no extra details needed.

The answer is False. Some of them “…stubbornly refused to believe and publicly maligned the Way…” (Acts 19:9) Three months of bold, persuasive talk didn't win over everyone in the room. Even so, Paul didn't quit. He just moved the conversation to a new place.

The answer is that Paul takes his disciples to the lecture hall of Tyrannus. The text says he “…took his disciples and left the synagogue to conduct daily discussions in the lecture hall of Tyrannus.” (Acts 19:9) He changes the location and keeps going. When one door closes, he finds the next one.

The answer is everyone in the province of Asia. The text says “…everyone who lived in the province of Asia, Jews and Greeks alike, heard the word of the Lord.” (Acts 19:10) That's a whole province, from one lecture hall and two years of daily discussions. The word got a lot farther than that one room.

The answer is handkerchiefs and aprons that had touched Paul. “…even handkerchiefs and aprons that had touched him were taken to the sick…” (Acts 19:12) The text says God did these extraordinary miracles through Paul's hands. Everyday cloth, and God did something extraordinary with it.
The answer is False. The text says “…the diseases and evil spirits left them.” (Acts 19:12) Both left, so it wasn't only the diseases. That's a full list, and God did all of it through Paul's hands.
The answer is Paul. The exorcists said, “I command you by Jesus, whom Paul proclaims.” (Acts 19:13) They pointed to Paul's preaching as their line. I think that's about to cause trouble.

The answer is that the spirit knows Jesus and knows about Paul but asks who they are. It says, “Jesus I know, and I know about Paul, but who are you?” (Acts 19:15) The sons of Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, get a question aimed right at them. It's a question nobody wants to get at work, let alone from that.

The answer is that they run out naked and wounded. The text says, “The attack was so violent that they ran out of the house naked and wounded.” (Acts 19:16) The seven sons of Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, are the ones who leave this way. This is a heavy part, and I think this one hurts.

The answer is True. “…fear came over all of them. So the name of the Lord Jesus was held in high honor.” (Acts 19:17) The news reached the Jews and Greeks living in Ephesus. After it, they treated His name with great respect.

The answer is that they confess and disclose their deeds. The text says, “Many who had believed now came forward, confessing and disclosing their deeds.” (Acts 19:18) These are people who had already believed, and they come forward anyway. That takes guts, friends, and I'd rather confess a burnt batch.

The answer is that they burn them in front of everyone. The text says “…a number of those who had practiced magic arts brought their books and burned them in front of everyone.” (Acts 19:19) When the value of those books was calculated, it came to fifty thousand drachmas. And they still did it in front of everyone.

The answer is True. “So the word of the Lord powerfully continued to spread and prevail.” (Acts 19:20) After the fear, the confessions and the burning books, the word kept on spreading. It keeps going with power. That's how this passage ends.
